diag.interference.current.one: On channel {channel} ({band}); {count} other network on the same channel
diag.interference.current.other: On channel {channel} ({band}); {count} other networks on the same channel

diag.interference.advice_5g: Try channel group {group} (fewest networks; channel {channel} is the emptiest).
diag.interference.advice_24g: Move to 5 GHz if the signal allows, or switch to whichever of channels 1/6/11 is least crowded.
diag.interference.advice_6g: 6 GHz has many channels: pick another one in the router's settings (or let it choose automatically), or use a narrower channel width.
diag.drops.title: Disconnect history (7 days)
diag.drops.by_day: Disconnects by the driver per day: {days}
diag.drops.bad: {count} disconnects by the driver in 7 days, last {ago}
diag.drops.warn: {driver} disconnects by the driver, {limited} limited-connectivity events
diag.drops.ok: No disconnects by the driver in 7 days
diag.drops.advice: Apply the power tweaks, update or roll back the driver, and turn on the watchdog.
diag.ping.title: Ping quality
diag.ping.no_data: Not enough data from the monitor yet (needs ≥ 60 samples in the last hour)

diag.ping.left_out.one: {count} minute left out: the network changed then
diag.ping.left_out.other: {count} minutes left out: the network changed then

diag.ping.router_loss: Packet loss to the router: a local problem (PC ↔ router / Wi‑Fi)
diag.ping.router_jitter: Unstable latency to the router (jitter above 30 ms): a local problem (PC ↔ router / Wi‑Fi)
diag.ping.wan_jitter: The router is fine but latency to the Internet is unstable (ping only, no TCP/HTTP data yet): an ISP/WAN problem, or ICMP is deprioritized
diag.ping.icmp_jitter: Pings to the Internet have unstable latency but TCP/HTTP connections are fine: ICMP is deprioritized, this is not an outage
diag.ping.icmp_limited: Pings to the Internet lose packets but TCP/HTTP connections are fine: ICMP is rate-limited, this is not an outage
diag.ping.wan_loss: The router is fine but TCP/HTTP connections to the Internet lose packets: an ISP/WAN problem
diag.ping.wan_loss_ping_only: The router is fine but the Internet loses packets (ping only, no TCP/HTTP data yet): an ISP/WAN problem, or ICMP is rate-limited
diag.ping.ok: Packet loss and jitter within limits
diag.ping.advice_router: Fix the Wi‑Fi first (see the signal, interference and antenna checks).
diag.ping.advice_icmp_limited: Nothing to fix. Ping to the Internet is not reliable on this network; go by the TCP/HTTP numbers.
diag.ping.advice_wan: The router is fine, so the fault is beyond it: check TCP/DNS (see the DNS check) or contact your ISP.
diag.dns.title: DNS benchmark
diag.dns.unknown_in_use: Could not tell which DNS server is in use
diag.dns.broken: The DNS in use has errors or timeouts: {servers}
diag.dns.advice_broken: Try another DNS (e.g. 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8) or check the router's DNS.
diag.dns.advice_promote: {server} is also configured and faster: make it the primary DNS.
diag.dns.advice_router_cache: The router answers fast from its cache, so this number is optimistic; compare with the fastest public DNS before switching.
diag.dns.slower: The DNS in use is about {gap:.0f} ms slower than {server}
diag.dns.ok: The DNS in use is fast and error-free

diag.tcp_ports.warn.one: {count} TCP port exhaustion event in 7 days
diag.tcp_ports.warn.other: {count} TCP port exhaustion events in 7 days

diag.tcp_ports.advice: Shorten TcpTimedWaitDelay (tweak tcp_timedwait, needs a restart).

diag.vpn.off: VPN software is installed but off
diag.vpn.none: No VPN or virtual adapter found
diag.wired.title: Wired network available
diag.wired.no_port: This PC has no LAN port
diag.wired.plugged: A network cable is plugged in
diag.wired.idle_port: A LAN port is free while you are on Wi‑Fi
diag.wired.advice: A LAN cable is the most stable option.
diag.wired.unplugged: The LAN port has no cable

diag.tweaks.unknown: Cannot assess: no tweaks are declared
diag.tweaks.ok: All low-risk optimizations are on or do not apply
diag.tweaks.advice: Open the Optimize tab to enable them one by one.
diag.wifi7_mlo.title: Wi‑Fi 7 / MLO compatibility
diag.wifi7_mlo.router_no_be: The router does not broadcast Wi‑Fi 7 (802.11be)
diag.wifi7_mlo.both: The router and the card both support Wi‑Fi 7
diag.wifi7_mlo.bands: The SSID in use '{ssid}' broadcasts on: {bands}
diag.wifi7_mlo.history: Last {hours}h: {bad}/{total} minutes with Rx ≤ 6 Mbps and packet loss ({fraction:.0%})
diag.wifi7_mlo.warn: The card does not support Wi‑Fi 7 but {where} broadcasts 802.11be, with speed collapses and packet loss
diag.wifi7_mlo.advice_warn: Turn off MLO/Wi‑Fi 7 on the router, or use an SSID compatible with Wi‑Fi 5/6.
diag.wifi7_mlo.note_same_ssid: the SSID in use also broadcasts 802.11be
diag.wifi7_mlo.note_other_ssid: this PC is on another SSID without 802.11be, so MLO has no effect yet
diag.wifi7_mlo.info: The router broadcasts Wi‑Fi 7 but the card does not; {note}
diag.wifi7_mlo.advice_info: If the connection drops or Rx collapses, turn off MLO on the router (EXP-009).
diag.modem_wifi.title: ISP modem Wi‑Fi (bridge mode)
diag.modem_wifi.advice: Turn off Wi‑Fi on the modem (WLAN button or admin page) and keep the router at least 1 m from the modem.
diag.modem_wifi.strong_family: A group of very strong unknown networks shares one MAC family: most likely the old modem still broadcasts Wi‑Fi
diag.modem_wifi.medium_family: A group of fairly strong unknown networks shares one MAC family
diag.modem_wifi.loud: A very strong unknown network (a transmitter nearby)
diag.modem_wifi.advice_loud: If it is your old modem/router, turn off its Wi‑Fi and keep it at least 1 m from the main router.
diag.physical_link.title: Poor physical link (antenna / placement)
diag.physical_link.not_enough: Not enough data ({count} connected minutes, needs ≥ {needed})
diag.physical_link.bad_minutes: {bad}/{total} minutes ({fraction:.0%}) had Rx ≤ 30 Mbps and ≥ 5% packet loss to the router
diag.physical_link.ok: Rx rate and packet loss to the router are stable
diag.physical_link.recent: Last 3 hours: {fraction:.0%} of minutes like that ({total} minutes)
diag.physical_link.improved: Speed collapses with packet loss happened in the last 24h but the last 3 hours are fine (improved?)
diag.physical_link.advice_improved: If you just moved the PC, the antenna or a setting, watch a few more hours to confirm.
diag.physical_link.weak_signal: The signal is very weak, so this is mostly distance or obstacles; see the signal check
diag.physical_link.warn: The Wi‑Fi link often collapses in speed with packet loss
diag.physical_link.info: Occasional speed collapses with packet loss
diag.physical_link.advice: This check cannot tell the cause. Rule out first: MLO/Wi‑Fi 7, an old modem's Wi‑Fi, channel interference, the driver. If those are clean, suspect a blocked card antenna (metal desk frame, PC case, cable bundle): turn or move the antennas into the open, or use an extension antenna; compare again after a few hours.
diag.path_mtu.title: Path MTU (large packets)
diag.path_mtu.no_interface: Cannot read the MTU of the network interface in use
diag.path_mtu.target: {target}: packets up to {mtu} bytes get through
diag.path_mtu.no_reply: No destination answered, so the path MTU cannot be measured
diag.path_mtu.ok: Packets of the full interface MTU ({mtu} bytes) get through
diag.path_mtu.too_big: The interface MTU ({mtu} bytes) is larger than the path allows ({path} bytes)
diag.path_mtu.pppoe: 1492 bytes is typical of a PPPoE Internet connection
diag.path_mtu.advice: Large packets can be dropped on the way, so pages hang half-loaded and downloads stall. Set the MTU of {name} to {path} (as Admin: netsh interface ipv4 set subinterface "{name}" mtu={path} store=persistent; for IPv6: netsh interface ipv6 set subinterface "{name}" mtu={path} store=persistent), or turn on MSS clamping on the router.
diag.path_mtu.no_ipv4: No IPv4 route to the Internet: this check measures IPv4 only
diag.path_mtu.capped: The interface MTU is above {cap} bytes (jumbo frames); the Internet carries at most {cap}, so the probe stops there
diag.path_mtu.ok_capped: Packets of {cap} bytes, the most the Internet carries, get through
diag.path_mtu.reported: Routers answer "packet too big", so Windows lowers the packet size by itself; large packets are not lost
diag.path_mtu.one_target: Only one destination answered and it may drop pings anyway, so the smaller path is not confirmed
diag.path_mtu.silent: Large packets vanish without any "packet too big" answer: connections can hang (PMTUD blackhole)
diag.bufferbloat.title: Bufferbloat (latency under load)
diag.bufferbloat.no_idle: Cannot measure: no ping replies from the Internet while idle
diag.bufferbloat.advice_retry: Check the network connection and run again.
diag.bufferbloat.weak_load: The {phase} load reached only {mbps:.1f} Mbps, not enough to fill the line
diag.bufferbloat.line: {label} during {phase} ({mbps:.0f} Mbps): median {median:.0f} ms, p95 {p95:.0f} ms, {delta:+.0f} ms added, {loss:.0f}% lost
diag.bufferbloat.no_result: Could not measure latency under load
diag.bufferbloat.advice_unreachable: Check the connection to speed.cloudflare.com (firewall/proxy) and run again.
diag.bufferbloat.ok: Latency barely rises when the line is busy (at most +{delta:.0f} ms)
diag.bufferbloat.loss_only: Median latency barely rises but pings to the Internet lose {loss:.0f}% when the line is busy (a full queue dropping packets)
diag.bufferbloat.where_local: , rising even to the router ⇒ the queue is on the PC ↔ router hop (saturated Wi‑Fi or an overloaded router)
diag.bufferbloat.where_wan: , not rising to the router ⇒ the queue is on the WAN hop (modem/router → ISP)
diag.bufferbloat.rise: Latency to the Internet rises {amount} when the line is busy{where}
diag.bufferbloat.advice: Turn on SQM / smart QoS (fq_codel or CAKE) on the router and set the upload/download limits about 5–10% below the real bandwidth. If the router has no SQM, lower the upload speed of the app causing the load.
diag.route.title: Route to far-away destinations
diag.route.no_data: Cannot compare routes: fewer than 3 reference sites answered
diag.route.tunnel_on: A VPN or tunnel is up, so the routes measured are the tunnel's, not the ISP's
diag.route.ok: Every reference site answers in a similar time (nearest {near:.0f} ms)
diag.route.detour: Some reference sites take a much longer path than the others (nearest {near:.0f} ms): {hosts}
diag.route.advice: This usually points at the ISP's route to those destinations, not at this PC. Nothing on the PC fixes it: a tunnel service may take a shorter path (but can slow nearby sites), or ask the ISP.
event.router_down.cut: PC could not reach router {router}; cut short by a monitoring gap
event.internet_down.local.cut: router also unreachable; cut short by a monitoring gap
event.internet_down.wan.cut: router reachable -> ISP/router WAN side; cut short by a monitoring gap
event.internet_down.wan.unstable: router reachable -> ISP/router WAN side; unstable: {drops} drops
event.monitor_gap: no samples for {seconds} s (sleep, hang or paused)
server.action.no_profile: The Wi‑Fi card or profile to reconnect is unknown
elevation.not_admin: The process does not have Administrator rights
elevation.unknown_tweak: There is no tweak '{tweak}' in the catalog
elevation.cancelled: Cancelled: Administrator rights were not granted
elevation.launch_failed: Could not start the Administrator process (error {error})
elevation.timed_out: The Administrator process did not finish in time
elevation.no_result: The Administrator process returned no result (exit code {exit_code})
watchdog.reason.verifying: waiting for the result of the previous action
watchdog.reason.other_uplink: another network path is in use (not Wi‑Fi)
watchdog.reason.grace: in the waiting period after the PC woke up or an optimization changed
watchdog.reason.ladder_done: every step was tried for this incident; waiting for the network to recover
watchdog.reason.hourly_cap: reached the cap of {count} actions per hour
watchdog.event.recovered_after: Network back {after}s after the action '{action}' (incident lasted {duration}s)
watchdog.event.ineffective: '{action}' did not help after {seconds}s ({count}/{limit} in a row)
watchdog.event.tripped: Watchdog turned itself off: {count} ineffective actions in a row. Turn it back on in settings once the cause has been checked.
watchdog.error.no_profile: the last Wi‑Fi profile is unknown
tweak.wifi_power_saving.name: Turn off the card's power saving
tweak.wifi_power_saving.note: A common cause of intermittent drops
tweak.wifi_wake_magic.name: Turn off Wake on Magic Packet
tweak.wifi_wake_magic.note: Keeps the card from being woken up or hanging during sleep
tweak.wifi_wake_pattern.name: Turn off Wake on Pattern Match
tweak.wifi_roaming.name: Reduce roaming
tweak.wifi_roaming.note: Less access-point hopping on mesh networks; Intel cards only
tweak.wifi_bw20_5g.name: 5 GHz bandwidth: 20 MHz only
tweak.wifi_bw20_5g.note: Lower top speed in exchange for stability where the air is crowded
tweak.wifi_mode_ac.name: Force Wi‑Fi 5 (802.11ac)
tweak.wifi_mode_ac.note: Try when you suspect a Wi‑Fi 6 compatibility problem between card and router
tweak.wifi_prefer_5g.name: Prefer the 5 GHz band
tweak.wifi_prefer_5g.note: Moves a card that clings to 2.4 GHz onto 5 GHz when it is in range, and still falls back to 2.4 GHz elsewhere. Offered only when your network has a 5 GHz access point
tweak.wifi_tx_power_max.name: Highest transmit power
tweak.wifi_tx_power_max.note: Keeps the card at its top transmit level instead of letting the driver lower it. Slightly more heat and battery use on a laptop
tweak.device_power_off.name: Don't let Windows turn off the card
tweak.device_power_off.note: Takes effect after restarting the card or the PC
tweak.power_wireless_max.name: Wireless Adapter: Maximum Performance
tweak.power_wireless_max.note: Applies to the current power plan only
tweak.power_pcie_aspm_off.name: Turn off PCIe ASPM
tweak.power_pcie_aspm_off.note: Important for PCIe cards (MediaTek MT7921/7922). Slightly higher power use
tweak.tcp_timedwait.name: Shorten TIME_WAIT
tweak.tcp_timedwait.note: Fewer port-exhaustion errors (Tcpip event 4227). The original value does not exist ⇒ restoring deletes the value
tweak.ipv6_off.name: Turn off IPv6 on Wi‑Fi
tweak.ipv6_off.note: Only try this when you suspect the router's IPv6 or IPv6 DNS slows things down
tweak.upload_shaping.name: Limit the upload speed to keep latency low under load
tweak.upload_shaping.note: Measures your upload first, then caps it at 85% so the queue stays on the PC instead of the modem. Upload only: the download direction can only be shaped on the router (SQM)
tweak.upload_shaping.value: limited to {limit:.1f} Mbps (85% of the {upload:.1f} Mbps upload measured)
tweak.upload_shaping.refused.weak: The measurement did not load the line enough ({mbps:.1f} Mbps, {samples} samples); try again
tweak.upload_shaping.refused.ceiling: The measurement reached its own limit ({mbps:.1f} of {ceiling:.0f} Mbps), so the line may be faster than it can tell; nothing was changed
tweak.upload_shaping.refused.not_needed: Latency rises only {rise:.0f} ms under upload; nothing to fix, so nothing was changed
tweak.upload_shaping.refused.bounds: A {cap:.1f} Mbps limit is outside the safe range ({low:.0f}–{high:.0f} Mbps); nothing was changed
tweak.tcp_ecn.name: Turn on TCP ECN
tweak.tcp_ecn.note: Experimental: routers can flag congestion instead of dropping packets, which may lower latency under load. Some devices in between mishandle ECN packets, so keep it off unless a before/after measurement shows a gain
tweak.rsc_off.name: Turn off Receive Segment Coalescing on the Wi‑Fi card
tweak.rsc_off.note: Experimental: received packets reach Windows one by one, which may lower latency at the price of a little throughput and more CPU use. Restoring needs the backup
tweak.packet_coalescing_off.name: Turn off the Packet Coalescing Filter
tweak.packet_coalescing_off.note: Experimental: the card stops holding back received packets to save power: lower latency, slightly more power use. Restoring needs the backup
tweak.dns_fastest.name: Use the fastest public DNS over HTTPS
tweak.dns_fastest.note: Measures Cloudflare, Google and Quad9 and uses the two fastest providers, encrypted with DoH. Turning it off brings the network's own DNS back. Not offered with a VPN, on a domain network, with a DNS suffix or behind a captive portal
tweak.reason.no_property: The card does not have this property
tweak.reason.not_connected: Not connected to a Wi‑Fi network
tweak.reason.bands_unknown: Windows' last scan does not show which bands '{ssid}' uses
tweak.reason.no_5ghz: '{ssid}' has no 5 GHz access point in range
tweak.reason.not_on_24ghz: Already connected on {band}; this only helps a card stuck on 2.4 GHz
tweak.reason.band_unknown: Cannot tell which band the Wi‑Fi connection is on
tweak.reason.driver_default: On because the driver ships that way; the tool did not set it, so there is nothing to turn off
tweak.reason.multi_value: '{property}' has a multi-part value, not supported
tweak.reason.needs_measurement: Needs a measurement of this network first
tweak.reason.no_default_registry: No backup, and the default value is unknown
tweak.reason.no_default_powercfg: powercfg has no known default value; a backup is needed
tweak.reason.no_default_tcp: No backup, and the default value is unknown
tweak.reason.no_rsc: This card does not support Receive Segment Coalescing
tweak.reason.no_default_rsc: No backup; the original setting of the card is unknown
tweak.reason.no_default_offload: No known default value; a backup is needed
tweak.reason.no_uplink: No network connection whose DNS could be changed
tweak.reason.dns_vpn: A VPN is up; it may need its own DNS
tweak.reason.dns_domain: This PC is on a domain or the network has a DNS suffix; internal names need the network's own DNS
tweak.reason.dns_static_v6: The network adapter has a static IPv6 DNS server, which restoring would erase
tweak.reason.dns_captive: The network looks like a captive portal (a sign-in page)
tweak.reason.dns_no_fast_servers: The benchmark did not find two public DNS providers that answer reliably; nothing was changed
tweak.reason.no_default_dns: No backup; the original DNS settings are unknown
tweak.reason.dns_other_interface: the saved original DNS settings belong to another network connection. Turn this off first, while that connection is in use
tweak.reason.dns_backup_elsewhere: On for another network connection ({name}), not the one in use now. Turn it off to put that connection's DNS back
tweak.reason.dns_interface_gone: The network connection whose DNS was changed is not available now (unplugged or removed)
tweak.reason.no_doh: This Windows has no DNS over HTTPS support (it needs Windows 11 or a recent Windows 10)
tweak.result.backup_unreadable_apply: backup.json is unreadable; not applying, so the original values cannot be lost: {error}
tweak.result.backup_write_failed: Cannot write backup.json; nothing was applied: {error}
tweak.result.no_effect: Applied, but reading it back shows it is still off
tweak.result.rollback_failed: {problem}; ROLLBACK FAILED — the backup is kept, turn this tweak off again
tweak.result.no_safe_default: No backup and no safe default value; left unchanged
tweak.result.driver_default: Already the driver's default; nothing to restore
tweak.result.default_restore_no_effect: Reset to the driver default, but the setting is still on
tweak.result.restore_failed: Restoring failed: {error}; the backup is kept
tweak.result.restore_mismatch: Restored, but the value does not match the backup; the backup is kept
tweak.result.measure_failed: Could not measure the connection (no load or no replies); nothing was changed
tweak.result.adopt_off: The tweak is off: the current value already is the original; not adopted
tweak.result.backup_exists: A backup already exists; keeping the old one
tweak.event.disabled_default: Optimization off: {name} (back to default, no backup)
tweak.event.backup_not_removed: {name}: restored, but the backup could not be removed: {error}
tweak.event.measurement_not_kept: {name}: applied, but the measurement could not be saved: {error}
tweak.event.verified_helped: {name}: latency rise under load {before:.0f} → {after:.0f} ms, it helped
tweak.event.verified_no_help: {name}: latency rise under load {before:.0f} → {after:.0f} ms, no clear improvement
tweak.event.verified_unknown: {name}: could not measure again after applying
tweak.verdict.helped: Latency rise under load went from {before:.0f} to {after:.0f} ms
tweak.verdict.no_help: Latency rise under load went from {before:.0f} to {after:.0f} ms — no clear improvement; consider turning it off
tweak.verdict.unknown: Could not measure again to check the effect
tweak.plan.will_apply: will: save the current value to backup.json (if not saved yet), then apply{disrupts}{reboot}
tweak.plan.will_measure: will: measure the connection first (~15 s of real traffic), refuse if there is nothing to fix, derive the value from it
tweak.plan.disrupts: — the card will restart and the network drops for a few seconds
tweak.plan.will_restore: will: restore the value saved in backup.json
tweak.plan.will_default: will: go back to the default value
tweak.plan.is_default: on by the driver's default, not set by the tool: nothing to turn off
tweak.plan.will_refuse: no backup and no safe default: will refuse
tweak.cli.dry_run: Nothing done. Add --apply to do it.
ui.language.hint: Translations other than English and Vietnamese are machine-made and still need a native speaker's review.
ui.state.router_down_detail: Wi‑Fi or the network card is not working · down for {duration}
ui.state.internet_down_detail: The router answers but the Internet does not · down for {duration}
ui.watchdog.title: Watchdog
ui.watchdog.description: Repairs the connection on its own when Wi‑Fi hangs, within strict limits.
ui.optimize.subtitle: Every change is backed up first and can be undone.
ui.optimize.disrupts: Network drops for a few seconds
ui.optimize.measured.upload_shaping: Limited to {limit:.1f} Mbps — 85% of the {upload:.1f} Mbps upload measured on {date}
ui.optimize.stale.hint: Turn it off and on again to measure this network
ui.sheet.experimental.title: Turn on an experimental tweak?
ui.sheet.experimental.body: “{name}” can lower speed or have side effects. The original value is backed up, so you can turn it off at any time.
ui.sheet.measured.title: Measure your connection first?
ui.sheet.measured.body: “{name}” measures your upload for about 15 seconds (up to 100 MB), before and after the change, and is not applied if there is nothing to fix.
ui.diag.bufferbloat_run: Measure (about 30 s, uses up to 200 MB)
ui.settings.notify_outages: Notify me when the connection drops
ui.settings.notify_after: Only after it has been down for {duration}
ui.settings.watchdog_dry_run: Dry run: only log what it would do
ui.mockup.banner: Mockup — sample data, nothing is applied
impact.collecting: Collecting data: {hours} h measured after the change, needs {needed} h
impact.no_baseline: No monitoring data from before the change to compare with
impact.no_change: No clear difference since the change
impact.metric.bad_link: Minutes with a collapsed Wi‑Fi link: {before:.0%} → {after:.0%}
impact.preliminary: Preliminary: {hours} h after the change; a fair comparison needs 24 h
impact.overlap: Another change was made within 24 hours, so their effects cannot be separated
impact.caveat: Measured, not proven: the router, busy hours or other devices can also explain a difference.
manual.antenna.title: Reposition the Wi‑Fi card's antennas
manual.antenna.body: Turn the antennas upright and move them out from behind the PC case or a metal desk frame, ideally with a clear line toward the router. If the PC sits under a desk, an antenna extension base helps.
manual.move_closer.title: Bring the PC and the router closer
manual.move_closer.body: Move the router or the PC so fewer walls are in between, or add a mesh node halfway. Use the 5 GHz network when the signal allows it.
manual.modem_wifi_off.title: Turn off the ISP modem's Wi‑Fi
manual.modem_wifi_off.body: When your own router handles Wi‑Fi, the modem's Wi‑Fi only adds interference. Turn it off with the WLAN button or in the modem's admin page, and keep the router at least 1 m from the modem.
manual.router_channel.title: Change the router's Wi‑Fi channel
manual.router_channel.body: In the router's admin page, pick the channel the diagnostics found least crowded instead of Auto.
manual.router_mlo_off.title: Turn off MLO / Wi‑Fi 7 on the router
manual.router_mlo_off.body: This card does not support Wi‑Fi 7. Turn off MLO in the router's settings, or connect to an SSID that runs Wi‑Fi 5/6 only.
manual.driver_update.title: Update or roll back the Wi‑Fi driver
manual.driver_update.body: Install the latest driver from the card maker's website, or roll back to a version that was stable (Device Manager → Properties → Driver → Roll Back).
manual.use_cable.title: Plug in a network cable
manual.use_cable.body: This PC has a free LAN port. A cable avoids every Wi‑Fi problem at once and is the most stable option.
manual.router_sqm.title: Turn on SQM / smart QoS on the router
manual.router_sqm.body: Most of the delay builds up on the download side, which only a router that shapes incoming traffic can control. Turn on SQM / smart QoS (CAKE or fq_codel) and set the limits about 5–10% below the real line speed. If the router has no SQM, OpenWrt (on routers that support it) offers one in the sqm-scripts package. If it still happens, the line itself is full and a faster plan helps.
manual.dns_server.title: Use another DNS server
manual.dns_server.body: The DNS server in use has errors or timeouts. Set a public one such as 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 in Windows or on the router.
manual.tunnel_route.title: Consider a tunnel for far-away destinations
manual.tunnel_route.body: Some destinations take a much longer path than others, which points at the ISP's route, not at this PC. A tunnel service you trust may take a shorter path to them, but it can slow down nearby destinations. Mark the step as done and the app compares the connection before and after; switch the tunnel off if it does not help.

apple.diag.bufferbloat.where_local: , rising even to the router ⇒ the queue is on the device ↔ router hop (saturated Wi‑Fi or an overloaded router)
apple.diag.physical_link.bad_minutes: {bad}/{total} minutes ({fraction:.0%}) had a transmit rate ≤ 30 Mbps and ≥ 5% packet loss to the router
apple.diag.physical_link.ok: The transmit rate and packet loss to the router are stable
apple.diag.physical_link.advice: This check cannot tell the cause. Rule out first: channel interference and the router's Wi‑Fi settings (MLO/Wi‑Fi 7, an old modem's Wi‑Fi). If those are clean, suspect what is around the Mac: metal, a closed lid, a dock or a display can block its antennas; move it into the open or closer to the router, and compare again after a few hours.
apple.diag.physical_link.advice_improved: If you just moved the Mac or the router, or changed a setting, watch a few more hours to confirm.
